label: Xenon-129, hyperpolarized, in vivo
reference: The 129Xe gas-phase resonance at 0 ppm (the inhaled xenon in the airspaces). Every dissolved-phase peak is quoted downfield of it, so all in vivo tissue values are large and positive. This is the in-vivo convention rather than the IUPAC one, which refers 129Xe to XeOF4; the two differ by a constant offset, and in-vivo work simply measures the gas peak in the same breath and calls it zero.
note: These lines come from two different experiments drawn on one axis: the gas, membrane and RBC values are the 3T pulmonary gas-exchange set, while the grey matter, white matter, CSF/fat and muscle lines are from head spectroscopic imaging at 1.5 to 3T. No single spectrum shows all nine. Dissolved-phase excitation is normally centered near 208 ppm, midway between the membrane and RBC peaks, and at 3T the 129Xe Larmor frequency is 35.3 MHz so 1 ppm is 35.3 Hz and the 20.6 ppm membrane-to-RBC gap is about 730 Hz, exactly half that at 1.5T.

peaks.name: RBC
peaks.note: 129Xe transiently bound to hemoglobin in the capillary bed. Multisite 3T healthy reference is 218.2 +/- 0.5 ppm, and standardized chemical shift imaging gives 217.9 ppm (217.2 to 218.5). Its position tracks blood oxygenation, moving downfield as sO2 rises: about 1 ppm per 10 percent sO2 near normal saturation and roughly 5 ppm across the full deoxygenated to fully oxygenated range. It therefore drifts about 1 ppm upfield over a 35 s breath hold, oscillates with the cardiac cycle at about 10 percent amplitude, and sits about 0.7 ppm lower in IPF.

peaks.name: RBC brain
peaks.full: Red blood cells in cerebral blood
peaks.note: The same hemoglobin-bound resonance seen in the lung, detected in the head and localized by chemical shift imaging to the Circle of Willis. Reported near 217 ppm at 1.5T; the small offset from the pulmonary value reflects cohort, field and fitting model, not a different chemical species. In rats the corresponding peak sits near 210 ppm.

peaks.name: CSF/fat
peaks.full: Blood plasma, cerebrospinal fluid and fat outside the brain
peaks.note: The most downfield of the four non-RBC head resonances, assigned by 1.5T head CSI to interstitial fluid and plasma, CSF, and extracranial fat. It is the brain-spectrum counterpart of the lung membrane peak and is not resolved from it at typical in vivo linewidths.

peaks.name: Membrane
peaks.full: Membrane (barrier), i.e. tissue plus blood plasma
peaks.note: 129Xe in alveolar epithelium, interstitium, capillary endothelium and plasma, all unresolved at clinical field. Multisite 3T healthy reference is 197.6 +/- 0.3 ppm; older papers round it to 197 or 198 ppm and call it barrier or tissue/plasma. Time-domain fitting of the FID shows it is really two components about 5 ppm apart with nearly opposite starting phase, but 1-point Dixon gas-exchange quantification treats it as a single peak. Healthy RBC:membrane amplitude ratio is about 0.49.

peaks.name: GM
peaks.note: The dominant brain-tissue resonance: 196 ppm at 1.5T, 196.5 ppm at 2.94T. Close to the 196 ppm shift of 129Xe dissolved in water, which is why aqueous compartments crowd this part of the spectrum. T2* about 8.8 ms at 1.5T, the longest of the dissolved peaks.

peaks.name: WM
peaks.note: Separated from gray matter by head CSI: 192 ppm at 1.5T, 193 ppm at 3T. The 4 ppm gray-to-white separation is only about 70 Hz at 1.5T, so the two are a shoulder on a whole-head spectrum unless the FID is fitted.

peaks.name: Muscle
peaks.full: Soft muscular tissue of the cheek, and midbrain/brainstem
peaks.note: The upfield edge of the head spectrum, assigned to extracranial soft muscular tissue and to 129Xe in the midbrain. Not a cerebral gas-exchange compartment; it is included in five-peak fits of brain spectra mainly so that it does not contaminate the white matter peak.

peaks.name: Gas
peaks.note: The inhaled gas and the frequency reference. In vivo it is roughly two orders of magnitude larger than any dissolved peak, so the height shown here is a drawing hint only; dissolved-phase spectra are acquired with a frequency-selective pulse about 200 ppm off resonance precisely to keep it out of the way.

peaks.name: Alveolar
peaks.note: The gas peak is not quite a singlet, and it is the alveolar component that holds still. Against the conducting-airway resonance taken as 0 ppm, the alveolar line sits about 2.2 ppm upfield and varies by only about 0.1 ppm between subjects, while the airway line itself ranges over roughly -0.6 to +1.3 ppm; the alveolar value is close to the -3 ppm or so predicted from the bulk susceptibility of a spherical air-tissue interface, which is why it is the better reference of the two. Separable only by careful time-domain fitting, and most pipelines report one gas peak at 0 ppm.

refNote: the gas-phase value, 11.777 MHz/T, not the bare-nucleus 11.860 in the isotope table; free xenon gas lies about 5300 ppm upfield of the IUPAC XeOF4 reference
